t: Soviet Luna probes reach the Moon
c: 1959 – The USSR and the US both launch probes to the Moon, but NASA's Pioneer probes all failed.

t: Frank Drake performs Project Ozma SETI experiment
c: 1960 – Cornell University astronomer Frank Drake performed the first modern SETI experiment, named "Project Ozma", after the Queen of Oz in L.

t: Chimpanzee Ham, Gagarin, and Shepard reach space
c: 1961 – As part of NASA's Mercury-Redstone 2 mission, the chimpanzee Ham becomes the first Hominidae in space.

t: John Glenn orbits Earth; Mariner 2 reaches Venus
c: 1962 – John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit Earth.

t: Maarten Schmidt identifies quasars as distant galaxies
c: 1963 – Dutch-American astronomer Maarten Schmidt measures the spectra of quasars, the mysterious star-like radio sources discovered in 1960.

t: Nikolai Kardashev develops civilization classification scale
c: 1964 – Nikolai Kardashev makes the Kardashev Scale to measure the power of civilizations.

t: Penzias and Wilson discover cosmic microwave background
c: 1965 – Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson announce the discovery of a weak radio signal coming from all parts of the sky.

t: Soviet Luna 9 soft-lands on Moon
c: 1966 – Soviet Luna 9 probe makes the first successful soft landing on the Moon in January, while the US lands the far more complex Surveyor missions, which…

t: Bell Burnell and Hewish detect first pulsar
c: 1967 – Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish detected the first pulsar, an object emitting regular pulses of radio waves.

t: Apollo 8 orbits the Moon with crew
c: 1968 – NASA's Apollo 8 mission becomes the first human spaceflight mission to enter the gravitational influence of another celestial body and to orbit it.

t: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin land on Moon
c: 1969 – The US wins the race for the Moon as Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin step onto the lunar surface on July 20.

t: USSR launches first space station Salyut 1
c: 1971 – The USSR launches its first space station Salyut 1 into orbit.

t: Charles Thomas Bolton proves black hole existence
c: 1972 – Charles Thomas Bolton was the first astronomer to present irrefutable evidence of the existence of a black hole.

t: Viking 1 and 2 land on Mars
c: 1976 – NASA's Viking 1 and Viking 2 space probes arrive at Mars.

t: NASA launches Voyager 2 space probe
c: 1977 – On August 20 the Voyager 2 space probe launched by NASA to study the Jovian system, Saturnian system, Uranian system, Neptunian system, the Kuiper belt,…

t: NASA launches Voyager 1 space probe
c: 1977 – On September 5 The Voyager 1 space probe launched by NASA to study the Jovian system, Saturnian system and the interstellar medium.

t: Space Shuttle Columbia makes first flight

t: IRAS infrared astronomy satellite launched
c: 1983 – The first infrared astronomy satellite, IRAS, is launched.

t: Space Shuttle Challenger explodes
c: 1986 – NASA's spaceflight program comes to a halt when Space Shuttle Challenger explodes shortly after launch.

t: Fleet of probes encounters Halley's Comet
c: 1986 – The returning Halley's Comet is met by a fleet of five probes from the USSR, Japan, and Europe.

t: Magellan probe arrives at Venus
c: 1989 – The Magellan probe, launched by NASA, arrives at Venus and spends three years mapping the planet with radar.

t: Hubble Space Telescope launched into orbit
c: 1990 – The Hubble Space Telescope, the first large optical telescope in orbit, is launched using the Space Shuttle, but astronomers soon discovered that it is…

t: COBE maps cosmic microwave background radiation
c: 1992 – The Cosmic Background Explorer satellite produces a detailed map of the background radiation remaining from the Big Bang.

t: Keck telescope completed on Mauna Kea
c: 1992 – The 10-meter Keck telescope on Mauna Kea, Hawaii, is completed.

t: Michel Mayor discovers first exoplanet 51 Pegasi b
c: 1995 – The first exoplanet, 51 Pegasi b, is discovered by Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz.

t: Universe's accelerated expansion discovered
c: 1998 – The accelerated expansion was discovered during 1998, by two independent projects, the Supernova Cosmology Project and the High-Z Supernova Search Team,…

t: Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrates on reentry
c: 2003 – Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrates upon reentry into Earth's atmosphere.

t: Mike Brown's team discovers Eris in outer solar system
c: 2005 – Mike Brown and his team discovered Eris a large body in the outer Solar System which was temporarily named as (2003) UB313.

t: IAU redefines planet and creates dwarf planet category
c: 2006 – International Astronomical Union (IAU) adopted a new definition of planet.

t: Suvi Gezari's team photographs supermassive black hole
c: 2012 – (May 2) First visual proof of the existence of black holes is published.

t: First extrasolar asteroid detected around white dwarf GD 61
c: 2013 – In October 2013, the first extrasolar asteroid is detected around white dwarf star GD 61.

t: ALMA telescope captures first image of HL Tauri
c: 2014 – The first image of a protoplanetary disk, HL Tauri, is taken by the ALMA telescope.

t: New Horizons encounters Pluto; LIGO detects gravitational waves

t: Proxima Centauri b discovered closest exoplanet to Solar System

t: Chang'e 4 lands on far side of Moon
c: 2019 – China's Chang'e 4 became the first spacecraft to perform a soft landing on the far side of the Moon.

t: Aleixo Garcia, first European in Inca lands
c: The Portuguese explorer Aleixo Garcia was the first European to reach the Inca Empire in 1524.

t: Túpac Inca begins northern conquests
c: Túpac Inca Yupanqui began conquests to the north in 1463 and continued them as Inca ruler after Pachacuti's death in 1471.

t: Shuar halt the Inca push into the Amazon
c: The empire's push into the Amazon Basin near the Chinchipe River was stopped by the Shuar in 1527.

t: Pizarro reaches Inca territory
c: Spanish conquistadors led by Francisco Pizarro and his brothers explored south from what is today Panama, reaching Inca territory by 1526.

t: 4,000 killed at Huayna Capac's death
c: As many as 4,000 servants, court officials, favorites and concubines were killed upon the death of the Inca Huayna Capac in 1527.

t: Manco Inca tries to escape the Spanish
c: The Pizarro brothers so mistreated Manco Inca that he ultimately tried to escape in 1535.

t: Manco retreats to Ollantaytambo
c: After ten months (see the Siege of Cuzco), Manco retreated to the nearby fortress of Ollantaytambo in 1537.

t: Titu Cusi leads the Vilcabamba resistance
c: In 1560, Sayri Túpac died suddenly, and his half-brother Titu Cusi Yupanqui took control of Vilcabamba and the Inca resistance to the Spanish.

t: Túpac Amaru becomes Inca
c: Túpac Amaru became the Inca ruler after Titu Cusi's sudden death in 1571.

t: First grammar of Quechua
c: The name quichua was first used in 1560 by Domingo de Santo Tomás in his Grammatica o arte de la lengua general de los indios de los reynos del Perú.

t: Atahualpa defeats Huáscar's armies
c: From 1531 to 1532, the armies fought many battles.

t: Pizarro explores South America's coast
c: In 1524–1526, the Spaniards, under the command of Francisco Pizarro, explored the northwestern coast of South America.

t: Huayna Capac dies of epidemic disease
c: Although Huayna Capac, who was in Tumebamba, did not personally encounter any Spaniards, he possibly contracted malaria or smallpox and died around 1527.

t: Spain turns the mit'a into mine labour
c: Mit'a was repurposed by the Spanish Crown in 1573, drafting one-seventh of the adult male population to work in mines.

t: First mit'a recruits arrive at Potosí
c: Under Toledo's leadership, the first mit'a recruits arrived in Potosí in 1573 from the regions directly surrounding the Potosí mine.

c: A young Mayta Capac was put in charge after his father died of old age.

t: Spain licenses Pizarro to conquer Peru
c: In 1529, Francisco Pizarro obtained permission from the Spanish Monarchy to conquer the land they called Peru.

t: Pizarro arrives in Peru
c: When Pizarro arrived in Peru in 1532, he found it vastly different from when he had been there just five years before.

t: Execution of Túpac Amaru, the last Inca
c: His son, Túpac Amaru, was the last Inca, being killed by the Spanish in 1572.

t: Almagro's expedition to Chile
c: Later in 1536, Almagro went on an expedition to Chile to find new regions.

t: Battle of Las Salinas: Pizarro v. Almagro
c: In 1538 was the Battle of Las Salinas, a fight between Pizarro and Almagro's men.

t: Viceroyalty of Peru created
c: In 1542, the Spanish created the Viceroyalty of New Castile, that shortly after would be called Viceroyalty of Peru.

t: Viceroyalty of Peru organized under Toledo
c: Nevertheless, the Viceroyalty of Peru was not organized until the arrival of a later Viceroy, Francisco de Toledo, in 1569.

t: Parthian Empire controls Mesopotamia
c: Around 150 BC, Mesopotamia was under the control of the Parthian Empire.

t: Recorded history begins in Mesopotamia
Cyrus the Great conquers Mesopotamia
c: In 539 BC, Mesopotamia was conquered by the Achaemenid Empire under Cyrus the Great.

t: Alexander the Great conquers Mesopotamia
c: The area was next conquered by Alexander the Great in 332 BC.

t: Esagil-kin-apli writes Diagnostic Handbook
c: The oldest Babylonian texts on medicine date back to the Old Babylonian period in the first half of the 2nd millennium BC.

t: Guennol Lioness sculpture created in Elam
c: The Guennol Lioness is an outstanding small limestone figure from Elam of about 3000–2800 BC, part man and part lion.

t: Masterpieces discovered at Royal Cemetery of Ur
Akkadian names first appear in texts
Kassite invasion marks Middle Babylonian period
c: The Middle Babylonian period started in the 16th century BC.

t: Carsten Niebuhr copies cuneiform texts
c: The Akkadian language began to be rediscovered when Carsten Niebuhr in 1767 was able to make extensive copies of cuneiform texts and published them in Denmark.

t: Baghdad founded as Abbasid Caliphate capital
c: With the rise of the Abbasid Caliphate in the mid-8th century, Iraq became the center of Islamic rule, with Baghdad, founded in 762, serving as the capital.

t: Iraq gains independence
c: Iraq gained independence in 1932 as the Kingdom of Iraq, which became a republic in 1958.

t: Hammurabi comes to power in Babylon
c: In 1792 BC, an Amorite ruler named Hammurabi came to power and immediately set about building Babylon into a major city, declaring himself its king.

t: Kassite Babylonia conquers Sealand Dynasty
Arabs and Chaldeans first mentioned
Nebuchadnezzar II succeeds Nabopolassar
c: Nebuchadnezzar II succeeded Nabopolassar in 605 BC.

t: Alexander defeats Persia, Greek rule begins
c: The Persian Empire fell to Alexander of Macedon in 331 BC and came under Greek rule as part of the Seleucid Empire.
